public_rationale: Zitron says GitHub Copilot loses hundreds of millions of dollars and makes very little revenue. Microsoft does not report Copilot revenue or profit. Its January 2026 call reported over 4.7 million paid Copilot subscribers, which suggests revenue is not trivial, though no dollar figure is given. Its April 2026 call said Copilot usage cut segment gross margin, and it announced usage-based pricing to match costs. That fits high costs but gives no loss amount. The only specific loss report I found is a 2023 WSJ per-user figure, which is outside the period. Without Copilot-level revenue and cost figures for 2025–2026, the size of any loss cannot be checked.
limitations: Microsoft does not break out Copilot financials.
'Fuck-all revenue' is hyperbole with no measurable threshold.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: GitHub Copilot loses hundreds of millions of dollars and generates little revenue.

statement.excerpt: Pale Horse: Any further price increases or service degradations from AI startups, and yes, that’s what I’d call GitHub Copilot, in the sense that it loses hundreds of millions of dollars and makes fuck-all revenue.

from_speaker: loses hundreds of millions of dollars
our_interpretation: Plain reading: around the time of the post, GitHub Copilot was running losses (costs above revenue) of at least a few hundred million dollars a year, and its revenue was small relative to those losses or to Microsoft's scale.

He named no period. I use the twelve months up to the post (April 2025 to April 2026) as the most recent period public evidence could cover. I picked a broad window rather than one quarter because 'hundreds of millions' reads as an annual scale. This is my choice and is flagged.
'Fuck-all revenue' is rhetorical. I read it as 'revenue too small to cover its costs', not as a literal claim of near-zero revenue.
criteria.support_condition: Credible figures (Microsoft disclosures or well-sourced reporting) show Copilot's costs exceeded its revenue by several hundred million dollars over a period around early 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible figures show Copilot was profitable or close to breakeven in the period, or that its losses were well below $100 million, or that its revenue was large relative to its costs.
